name: Terraform nested block bindings
summary: Let Terraform parts and anchors bind named nested blocks of a resource, verify sibling-block anchors by intra-resource name links, and allow a direct child to share its infrastructure container address.

changes.subject: vKEsyHFk/6E6hL0Zk#wYcdVszt
changes.value: Local CLI and HTTP adapters share canonical reads, edits, subject claims, proposals, migration, archive retention, and recovery. Legacy decoding serves explicit migration and exact retained originals. Semantic checks recognize Terraform nested-block addresses in containment and exempt at most one direct child sharing its parent container infrastructure address from BINDING_SHARED.

changes.subject: vKEsyHFk/6E6hL0Zk#6a2R1ddu
changes.value: The existing code opener also resolves an explicit migration preview before opening the candidate module binding. It refuses stale plans rather than using installed or legacy subjects. A file an agent's answer names opens as the binding it would be, in the innermost checkout that the vault reads and that holds it. Any other path opens nothing. For Terraform bindings, including local-module nested blocks, it resolves the checkout-contained module file and line through symbolLocation before launching.

changes.subject: vKEsyHFk/vKEsyHFk#8XKRkSHl
changes.value: Modules own their outgoing relationships. Independent flow collections describe exchanges. Compact proposals—including active drafts reconciled against the branch footprint—and authored narratives refer to stable subjects, while exact history lives in the signed archive.

changes.subject: vKEsyHFk/HBlhIeSD#5SMX69gS
changes.value: The checker reads current architecture, one selected state, or independent drafts, reporting bindings, anchors, declared relationships, interfaces, module depth, and document references with canonical identities. It reads every bound module interface across all languages it holds and hands Module depth what it read; EXPOSED_UNUSED warns when every use in that language resolved with no drawn outside caller, else reports information. The answer marks branch-touched modules and carries the model shallow-module setting; severities never depend on caller flags. Its state reader also reads a selected state at a source ref for branch footprint; Git locality and footprint use separate history operations, and language server timings name the program and TypeScript read. An anchor on a Terraform declaration neither end holds is judged per instance: unlisted declarations support when one instance reaches both ends (or descendants) without emitting undrawn evidence, and listed joins check roles per instance—supporting either orientation, warning ANCHOR_MISMATCH when every instance rules out the pair, withholding when an opaque end leaves room, and never falling back to self on pure links. For Terraform nested blocks, anchor support accepts 1-hop intra-resource name-linked sibling blocks (anchor-only, still warning on whole-resource anchors for nested-block ends), ownership attributes references in bound nested blocks to those parts and prefers a direct child sharing its parent infrastructure address, duplicate literal names report ambiguity in symbol-missing warnings, and dynamic, computed-name, or plan-only nested selectors skip with expression-not-followed.

changes.subject: vKEsyHFk/XppR9owz#bLpk2XKU
changes.value: Each command family keeps its contracts and handlers in a folder of src/cli/commands; the command table in routing/operations/run.ts registers them, and Contract execution calls the handlers. Check command help documents Terraform nested-block bindings, the runner restriction to top-level resources, expression-not-followed skips for dynamic or plan-only nested selectors, and the direct-child infrastructure exception to BINDING_SHARED.

changes.subject: vKEsyHFk/vKEsyHFk#DmbKboxU
changes.value: Owns canonical model schemas, positional Terraform address parsing (including depth-1 resource nested-block selectors), containment and infrastructure duplicate-binding rules, and vault persistence.

changes.subject: vKEsyHFk/vKEsyHFk#6HYaX0mK
changes.value: Owns code-fact extraction, Terraform nested-block parsing and sibling-link verification, symbol location lookup through the code-facts API, code-check evidence ownership, and history lenses.

changes.subject: vKEsyHFk/vKEsyHFk#7hdbqGFn
changes.value: Resolves and opens module bindings and file links in local editors, including route status projections and checkout-contained Terraform local-module nested-block targets.

changes.subject: vKEsyHFk/6E6hL0Zk#mR7wPSei
changes.value: Reads permitted source files through a content-hashed cache and carries adapter-extracted facts—including logic counts, computations, Terraform intra-resource sibling links, and ambiguous duplicate block symbols—into resolved SyntaxFacts.

changes.subject: vKEsyHFk/6E6hL0Zk#3CaBjhIM
changes.value: Module exposure reads every language that a module holds, not only the first one that matches. Each grammar query also names the kind of each export, the pieces of logic in each body, and the expression around each use of a name that another file defines. For Terraform, provider rules name the declarations that join two others: the evidence kind, the arguments for each end, and whether the declaration itself stands for an end that no argument resolves (true for triggers and pull subscriptions, false for pure links). Azure adds directed configured-path rules for subnet NAT gateway associations, diagnostic settings (excluding credential arguments), private DNS zone virtual network links, and NAT gateway public IP associations; undirected NSG filter attachments stay unlisted. Terraform addresses parse by position so trailing nested-block selectors (<resource>.<block_type>["name"]) stay distinct from instance keys; depth-1 resource nested blocks with literal name emit as visibility "block" definitions without pulling references or runners off the resource; 1-hop intra-resource sibling links store resolved block symbols only; duplicate literal names flag ambiguity; and dynamic, computed-name, or plan-only nested selectors are marked unfollowed.
